audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly claims Vladimir has no Sanguine Pool before level 6 - 'No Sanguine Pool exists yet', 'at 6 he gains Sanguine Pool the same level you get Feast', 'the only window your combo can't be pooled out of'. Sanguine Pool is his W and is available from level 2.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is listed as the W slot with a rank-1 cooldown of 28s. His level-6 ability is Hemoplague (120s). The page built its entire early-game and level-6 plan on an ability timing that does not exist, and it never states the interaction that actually decides the matchup: Feral Scream is a silence, so silencing him before he sinks denies the pool cast outright.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool is available from level 2 on 28/25/22/19/16s. Silence first, then commit; his level-6 spike is Hemoplague, a 120s damage amp that heals him per champion hit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Cho'Gath the first item and two-item stages and called level 6 a Skill stage, off the back of the false 'pool arrives at 6' premise.
audit.why: With the pool timing corrected, level 6 is Cho'Gath's - Feast is true damage his MR cannot reduce - while levels 4-5 and the two-item stage belong to Vladimir's scaling. The packet chart already reflects that and the 50.67% win rate over 594 games supports an even lane overall.
audit.corrected: Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Vladimir / Cho'Gath / Skill / Vladimir with ratings 5,6,6,4,6,5,4. Difficulty stays EVEN 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes were tied to the imaginary level-6 pool and to a fabricated percent-health E.
audit.why: His real curve is Transfusion's cooldown collapsing 9 to 4.6s, Sanguine Pool's 28 to 16s, and Crimson Pact converting AP into health as he buys AP.
audit.corrected: Levels 2-3 are yours on a 28s pool; 6 is yours on Feast's true damage; two items is his on Crimson Pact scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was listed as an item note but never tied to which abilities heal him.
audit.why: Transfusion and Hemoplague both carry the heal flag, and Hemoplague heals per champion hit, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended fights and teamfights, not just lane.
audit.corrected: Named Transfusion and Hemoplague as the heal sources and MR plus Grievous Wounds as the answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood being blocked by enemy units was never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's own description says the released blood 'can be blocked by enemy units', so keeping a minion between you removes his only lane poke.
audit.corrected: Stated as a do: stand behind minions and Tides of Blood does not reach you.

edits.before: Pre-6 neither of you has a real kill threat, but the key fact is Vlad has no Sanguine Pool yet — this is the only window where your combo can't be pooled out of. Throw Rupture at where he'll step to E you (not as a poke he strolls out of), then immediately Feral Scream to silence both his Q Transfusion heal and his E Tides of Blood charge, and walk. You sustain the trade back with Carnivore last-hits and Vorpal Spikes. Don't free-cast Rupture or let him E you uncontested — his Tides of Blood poke charges up and adds real chip if you ignore it.
edits.after: Neither of you has a real kill threat before 6, and the key fact is a sequencing one: Sanguine Pool is live from level 2 on a 28-second cooldown, but Feral Scream is a silence, so if you scream first he never casts it. Lead with the silence when he steps up to E you, then Rupture the knockup and walk, because the same silence also blanks his Transfusion heal and his Tides of Blood charge. Stand behind a minion while you farm: Riot's own text says the released blood is blocked by enemy units, so a caster minion eats his entire poke pattern for free.

edits.before: By 4-5 your Carnivore sustain, Vorpal Spikes waveclear, and Q-into-W combo stabilize you against a pre-Rylai Vlad who has no slow to stick to you. At 6 you both spike: Feast adds a true-damage execute that ignores his MR, but the catch is Sanguine Pool arrives the same level — the moment you Rupture or commit R, he pools untargetable and every one of those targeted casts whiffs while he heals off the pool. Bait the pool first (make him burn it dodging a Rupture or fearing the Feast threat), then all-in into its long early cooldown.
edits.after: By 4-5 Transfusion's cooldown has fallen toward 4.6 seconds and Tides of Blood chips you from 600 range, so this stretch is his - farm behind minions and give nothing. At 6 the lane swings: Feast is true damage his MR cannot reduce. The whole all-in is an order-of-operations problem. Sanguine Pool is 2 seconds of untargetable that eats a targeted execute, so Feral Scream must land before he sinks, not after. Silence, Rupture, execute. If he pools early to dodge a Rupture, that is 16 to 28 seconds with no escape at all.

edits.before: This is where the lane slips to him. Two AP items in, Vlad becomes a pool-kiting drain mage, and his E Tides of Blood deals percent-max-HP magic damage — that scales WITH the very HP your Feast stacks pile on, so being a giant actively feeds his poke instead of tanking it. He pools your Rupture, your silence, and your execute on demand and heals it all back with Transfusion. You stay a top-tier teamfight anchor — your Rupture knockup and Feral Scream silence are huge for your carries — but the straight 1v1 is his. Group, lock his backline with your CC, and don't try to solo a fed Vlad.
edits.after: This is where the lane slips to him. Two AP items in, Crimson Pact converts every point of that ability power back into bonus health, so he is a drain mage who is also durable, and Tides of Blood chips you from 600 while Transfusion tops him back up on a 4.6-second cooldown. Hemoplague makes it worse in a group fight: 120 seconds, it amplifies the damage you take for its duration, and it heals him for every champion it catches. You stay a top-tier teamfight anchor - the Rupture knockup and the Feral Scream silence are enormous for your carries - but bring Grievous Wounds and MR, and don't try to solo a fed Vlad.

notes: Two fabrications removed. (1) The page said Sanguine Pool arrives at level 6; it is his W, live from level 2. (2) The page twice claimed Tides of Blood deals 'percent-max-HP magic damage that scales WITH your Feast stacking'. There is no percentHealth flag on his E and Riot's description says only that he pays health to charge an area hit blocked by enemy units - I removed the claim rather than soften it. Crimson Pact runs the other way: HIS bonus health becomes HIS ability power. Separately, chogath.json tags Rupture (Q) with grounding, which is a tooltip-parse misfire on the words 'Ruptures the ground' (same false positive on Malphite Q and Olaf Q); I wrote the knockup only. The packet suspectName 'No Sanguine Pool' is a false positive on the name itself, but the sentence containing it was factually wrong for the reason above.
